samples.reason: This is an extraction and structured presentation task requiring clear comparative formatting of salary data. Plover scores significantly higher on Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 78.5) and Summarization (86.4 vs 79.9), both relevant for organizing comparative reference information. The creative decision-making about presentation structure is secondary to the core information synthesis task.

This is an open-ended informational task requiring extraction of salary data and creative decisions about presentation structure. Plover outperforms Willet on both relevant internal evals — Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 78.5) and Creative Generation (84.7 vs 81.2) — and has substantially stronger public benchmarks. The content is not harm-adjacent, so Willet's generative-work preference advantage (which doesn't translate to measured quality gains) doesn't outweigh Plover's capability edge.

This is an extraction, retrieval, and structured summarization task requiring the model to pull salary data for four job roles and organize it into a clear comparative format. Plover scores significantly higher on Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 78.5) and Summarization (86.4 vs 79.9), making it the better fit for synthesizing reference information into a clean, useful presentation.

This is a straightforward informational task involving data extraction and structured presentation. Plover has meaningfully higher scores on Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 78.5) and Summarization (86.4 vs 79.9), which align well with compiling and clearly presenting comparative role information. While Willet has a self-reported appetite for generative latitude, that's a preference dimension rather than a capability advantage, and the task is primarily informational rather than open-ended invention.

This is a creative-structured presentation task with extraction/retrieval components. Plover scores higher on both Creative Generation (84.7 vs 81.2) and Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 78.5), and the open-ended framing ("take the lead," "your call") benefits from a model that can synthesize information into a clear comparative format. The content is neutral, so Willet's strong harm-adjacent aversion profile—which is its defining preference characteristic—is irrelevant here. Plover's higher capability scores on the relevant dimensions make it the better choice.
